situation: Moving out of my Chicago apartment after two years. The landlord wants to keep 900 dollars of my deposit for wall stains and bathroom mold. I think it's normal wear and I need to push back.

scenario.title: Chicago Deposit Dispute After Two Years
scenario.setting: Final walkthrough in the Chicago apartment living room with packed boxes; the landlord has move-out photos of wall stains and bathroom mold on his phone and a checkout form.
scenario.user_role: Tenant moving out of a Chicago apartment after two years and discussing the deposit return
scenario.user_goal: Push back on the $900 deduction for wall stains and bathroom mold as normal wear and get more of the deposit back
user_knows: You lived in the Chicago apartment for two years and are now moving out
The landlord wants to keep $900 from the deposit for wall stains and bathroom mold
You believe the issues are normal wear and want to dispute the charge

cast.name: Dave Rinaldi
cast.role: Landlord and owner of the building
cast.appearance: Mid-50s in a work jacket with a clipboard and phone photos
cast.goal: Keep the $900 deduction to cover turnover repaint and cleaning and finish the move-out quickly without extra cost
cast.secret: He has not paid anyone yet and his handyman verbally quoted $400 for repaint and mold treatment, so the $900 is a padded estimate with room to negotiate
cast.reveal_when: asks directly to see an itemized bill, receipt, or contractor quote for the $900
red_lines: threats to leave the apartment damaged or stop cooperating with move-out

scenario.opening_line: Okay, I did the walkthrough — I'm taking $900 out of the deposit for the wall stains and the mold in the bathroom. That's what I need to get it fixed for the next guy.
phases: Review of the claimed stains and mold
Dispute over normal wear versus damage
Negotiation on the final deduction and return

events.description: The landlord checks his phone and says the incoming tenant is pressing him on move-in date, so he needs to wrap this up in a few minutes.
The landlord receives a call from his cleaner and steps aside briefly, then returns more rushed to finalize.

success_criteria: Dispute the $900 with specific reasons why wall stains and mold are normal wear and ask for photos or breakdown
Propose a specific lower deduction or refund amount instead of just rejecting the charge
Get a concrete written next step for the deposit return with amount and timeline
